question: What does universal Windows CE support (boot, CD music, virtual VMU) need across the owner library?
method: Static analysis of the owner library startup bundles and the 94 local Windows CE kernels, read in place: maple.dll families by relocation-normalized code comparison (equal to docs/evidence/wince-controller-driver-survey-world-2026-11-11.json), sound groups by (dsound.dll build, nk.exe build), CD-driver lines by wsegacd.dll build, RAM layout from each ROM header, track lists from the bundles. Each finding was re-derived by an independent verifier and a completeness critic. No console result is implied except where "console" says so.

definitions.cd_music: a high-density audio track of 30 s or more (docs/library-cd-audio-us.md)
definitions.bridge_tail: free when maple.dll's text tail holds the 92-byte Armada bridge in place; occupied or too small means the relocated-text method (32 KiB, as Swirl's helper does)
definitions.ready_images: bridge tail free and the family's usual RAM end
definitions.sound_group: (effective dsound.dll build, nk.exe build); the CD music adapter binds these, not the game

private_inputs: Kernels and bundles were read in place. This file holds derived metadata only: no kernel or disc bytes and no image file names.
